newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - June 18.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - June 18.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

QNI's shares were suspended on Tuesday ahead of an announcement today. Rumours circulated that South African group Gencor Ltd would launch a takeover bid for QNI or buy a large stake in the nickel producer at prices as high as A$3.40. Gencor and QNI have not commented, but QNI is expected to make an announcement after a board meeting later on Wednesday.
* Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$19.30 (+0.40)

Shell Canada Ltd said on Tuesday it found a partner in BHP Minerals to help plan the development of its proposed C$1 billion ($722 million) northern Alberta oil sands mining project. Shell Canada, the Canadian integrated oil arm of Royal Dutch/Shell Group, said BHP agreed to work on a pre-feasibility study for the Lease 13 project, expected to produce 120,000 to 150,000 barrels of bitumen a day starting in 2002.

Canada's Molson Cos Ltd and Australia's Foster's Brewing Group Ltd are said to be in talks to buy 20 percent of Molson Breweries from U.S. brewer Miller. A document prepared recently for the sale of a major parcel of Foster's shares reveal that talks with Miller, a unit of Philip Morris Cos Inc, are at an "advanced stage".

Industrial products and services provider Campbell Brothers Ltd said on Wednesday it was keen on making further acquisitions, particularly in its core business areas of soap, chemicals and laboratory services.
Pay television giant BSkyB Plc will enter the 200-channel digital era under a new leader after chief executive Sam Chisholm said on Tuesday he was stepping down on health grounds.
Shares in mining group Rio Tinto Plc in London reached a record high on Tuesday as copper prices continued to strengthen. -- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
